belief: I should be further along by now.
origins: Comparison is a quiet thief. Classmates’ promotions, social media updates, a parent’s expectations, or an internal timeline we set long ago can make us feel behind. Setbacks, caregiving, health, or career changes can slow us down, yet we measure ourselves against a straight line that few people actually walk.
teaches: Scripture says that to everything there is a season and a time for every purpose under heaven. David prays, “My times are in Your hands.” Paul wrote, “Forgetting what is behind and reaching forward to what is ahead, I press on toward the goal.” He also says that He who began a good work in us will carry it on to completion. God works on His own timetable, and the Bible’s heroes, from Moses to Joseph, often seemed far behind before God moved. Being “behind” is a measurement by the wrong ruler.
self_statements: Everyone my age is ahead of me.
I have wasted so much time.
I should have achieved more by now.
It is too late to catch up.
I am behind in every area.
I will never reach where others are.
errors: Insisting that I should be at a certain place by a certain age.
Measuring my life against other people’s highlights.
Believing that I am either on schedule or a failure.
questions: Who set the timeline I am measuring myself against?
What have I accomplished and learned in the years I think were “wasted”?
Whose path am I comparing myself to, and what do I not know about it?
What does God’s timing look like in the lives of people in Scripture?
What season am I in right now?
What is one step forward I can take?
truth: My times are in God’s hands. The timeline I am measuring against is not His. I can look at where I have been, receive where I am, and press on toward what is ahead without condemning myself for the pace.
hw_truths: My times are in God’s hands.
There is a season for everything.
I have grown more than I realize.
God carries His work to completion.
I can press on from here.
log: Where I am, not where I should be
Each week, write one thing you have learned or gained in this season and one step you took.
actions: Write where you thought you should be and who or what set that target.
List what you have learned or become in the last five years.
Take a break from checking others’ updates for a week.
Decide on one forward move this month.
prayer: Father, my times are in Your hands. Forgive me for measuring myself by a timeline You did not give. Help me press on from where I am with thankfulness and trust. Amen.
hw_questions: What have I learned in these years?
Whose life am I comparing mine to?
What can I thank God for?
What is one step this month?
name_example: Sarah can write: “My times are in God’s hands, so I can press on from where I am.”
